quotes.text: So a relationship isn't a formula and it isn't decoration you add at the end. It's a pathway, and every number in your report is only as trustworthy as the paths that lead into it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes relationships as the foundation of every reported number.

quotes.text: Keep bidirectional relationships to a minimum and switch one on only when you actually need it
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear, actionable modeling rule.

quotes.text: Nothing in power BI has a checkbox that says this is a fact table. The relationship itself decides the role.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains a surprising point about how fact and dimension roles emerge.

quotes.text: The habit that prevents most of this is unglamorous. Build the star. Keep one active, one to many. Link between each pair of tables and read the diagram before you blame the data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Condenses the episode's best practice into one habit.

quotes.text: One thing a relationship will never do is tell you that a number is wrong. It has no opinion about whether a result makes sense, that judgment stays with you.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sets honest expectations about what modeling can and cannot do.

Where beginners get burned and what relationships can't do
Semantic models, Fabric and storage modes

takeaways: A Power BI relationship is a filter pathway built on one shared column, and when the same number appears in every row the tables are usually not connected or not passing filters.
Cardinality decides which side leads, single cross filter direction is the safe default, and only one active path may exist between two tables, so role-playing dates need copies or a formula.
A star schema with one-to-many links from dimensions to facts keeps models fast and predictable, but relationships move filters and never fix bad data or wrong numbers.
hook: Power BI reports can look finished and still show wrong numbers because tables are not related correctly. This episode helps beginners and report builders understand relationships, cardinality, filter direction and the star schema so they can predict what every click does to their numbers.
